title: fragment-coalesce-transient-fallbacks-for-multi-stream-decode
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We are seeing non-deterministic decode failures and rare correctness regressions when concurrent prefill and decode streams cause fragmented CUDA graph captures across heterogeneous batch profiles. The root cause surface includes mismatched kernel selection heuristics between capture and replay paths, KV cache epoching differences, and capture boundary misalignment for short prefills.

Objective: Implement a runtime approach that (1) coalesces small/fragmented capture segments into stable 'cohorts' for deterministic replay where feasible, (2) provides a fast transient kernel fallback mode for any capture/replay mismatch that preserves correctness at slightly higher latency, and (3) adds a low-overhead validation harness and metrics to detect drift and trigger recapture heuristics automatically.

Why unique: Rather than forcing coarse-grained capture or conservative kernel lockstep, this ticket introduces a hybrid strategy that reduces unnecessary recaptures, keeps GPU occupancy high for common workloads, and guarantees correctness via safe fallbacks and deterministic verification.

Scope: Runtime (inference engine), capture controller, metrics/telemetry, canary rollout in Dedicated pools. Excludes API surface changes and user config exposure (later work).
acceptance_criteria: No silent correctness regressions in 1e5 synthetic replay tests across variable prefill lengths (1-512 tokens)
End-to-end error rate from capture/replay mismatches reduced to <0.01% on high-fragment workloads compared to baseline
Transient fallback path adds <6ms p50 latency for affected requests and <25% p99 overhead in worst-case scenarios
Metric telemetry (capture_drift_count, cohort_coalesce_ratio, transient_fallback_count) emitted and visible in runtime dashboard
Automatic recapture triggers after 3 drift detections per 10k requests, configurable via private release flags
approach: 1) Fragment detection: extend capture controller to fingerprint capture segments (op sequence, kernel hints, occupancy vector) at compile-time and runtime to detect fragmentation hotspots.

2) Cohort coalescing: when multiple short/adjacent captures are observed within a short epoch and share compatible fingerprints, merge them into a single cohort capture that replays deterministically across streams.

3) Transient kernel fallback: implement a lightweight fallback path that detects kernel-unavailable or mismatch at replay-time and runs a validated, slower kernel variant without requiring recapture (keeps output deterministic).

4) Validation harness: embed an optional fast verifier that replays a short token suffix on the host (or smaller device kernel) to confirm correctness before returning streamed tokens in ambiguous cases.
5) Heuristics & scoring: add a scoring model that chooses between coalescing, conservative recapture, or transient fallback based on estimated recapture cost vs expected recurrence probability.
6) Metrics & alerts: emit fine-grained telemetry and add Grafana panels and alert rules for capture drift and fallback rates.
7) Rollout: behind private runtime flag -> internal canary (Dedicated test pool) -> staged Tenancy rollout with rollback hooks and traffic slicing
milestones: M1: Spec and proto (capture fingerprint schema + fallback API) - 2025-02-17
M2: Cohort coalescing POC + unit tests - 2025-02-28
M3: Transient kernel fallback implementation + integration tests - 2025-03-07
M4: Validation harness and telemetry dashboards - 2025-03-12
comments: 2025-02-11 - Aisha Kapoor: Spiked fragment fingerprinting using op-seq + kernel-hash. Initial microbench shows that ~18% of captures in tail workloads are <4 ops and are causing high recapture churn.
2025-02-14 - Marco Nguyen: Added scoring heuristic draft. Decided to prefer coalescing for prefills <8 tokens if kernel hints match and occupancy delta <12%.
2025-02-20 - Design review (internal): Agreed that validation harness should be optional and cost-limited; it will run only on unstable replays or when fallback occurs >1/10000.

2025-02-25 - PR #rlw/runtime/graph-cohort (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2741): POC for cohort coalescing. Benchmarks attached to PR show 7% token throughput improvement for short-prefill HTTP workloads.

2025-03-01 - QA: Synthetic fuzz-run 100k cases across prefills 1..512. Observed 14 mismatches where fallback correctly preserved outputs. Need to reduce false-positive fallback triggers (currently at 0.5% of requests).
2025-03-03 - Marco Nguyen: Tweaked fallback trigger window and added a debounce to avoid flapping. Planning canary next week on dedicated-staging pool.
2025-03-04 - Performance note: Transient fallback path median latency +4.2ms, p99 +18ms on A100. This meets the transient SLA target; still optimizing p99 via kernel micro-tuning.
